summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with a history of HCV and alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatic encephalopathy, and depression was admitted for right upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. She had elevated lactate and tachycardia, likely due to volume depletion from recent emesis. Imaging showed cirrhosis but no evidence of obstruction, appendicitis, or colitis. A colonoscopy revealed a polyp in the descending colon, which was removed, with no active inflammation. Her symptoms resolved during the stay, and she was discharged home with a diagnosis of resolved gastroenteritis and functional abdominal pain. She was restarted on lactulose, given a short course of pain medication, and instructed to follow up on pending lab results and polyp pathology.
